Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

county noun

also counties, shire, county town

medieval

M-O s.v. political division: county; county (domain of count)

comitātus, comitātūs m.

noun, fourth declension

a county

From comes, a count: the land a count governed, and so an English shire (Lüders 1826, of Dorset and Gloucestershire) and a subdivision of a US state (M-O). Classically comitātus is an escort, a retinue (Lewis & Short), so make the sense clear the first time.

Other words

  • pāgus, pāgī m. — a country district, a canton

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.12.4: in quattuor pāgōs dīvīsa est

    Caesar’s word for the districts into which a Gallic people was divided, the nearest classical thing to a county; also the country as against the town, and the villagers themselves (Lewis & Short). A county council: see council.

Examples

  • nam omnis cīvitās Helvētia in quattuor pāgōs dīvīsa est

    for the whole Helvetian state is divided into four districtsCaes. BG 1.12.4

See also area, province, council, state.

SourcesLewis & Short: comitatus · Lewis & Short: pagus
